Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.

This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant genes in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture coordinating antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages, providing a framework for understanding extreme salinity tolerance in plants.

Lung cancer management 2026-12-01 Medium

An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.

This study applies an integrative systems-biology approach to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets for LSCC. The work highlights the value of combining transcriptomics with network analysis to detect systemic signals of cancer beyond the tumor microenvironment.

Cell reports methods 2026-11-16 Medium

Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.

The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating how accurately the learned network structures capture causal gene-gene relationships. The work addresses a gap in widely available software for both Bayesian network learning and structural causal assessment in this context.

Cell reports methods 2026-11-16 Medium

Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.

COAST is a new computational method that aligns consecutive tissue sections from spatial multi-omics experiments using only their associated images, without requiring shared molecular features or prior annotations. It was validated on spatial transcriptomics slides across different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, achieving performance comparable to established single-modality alignment tools. This enables reliable construction of unified multi-modal molecular datasets for downstream spatial analyses.

A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.

This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing to build a transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis inflorescence stem, revealing the endodermal gene regulatory network that drives gravitropism. The authors identify how the transcription factor SGR5/IDD15 links gravity perception in endodermal statocytes to asymmetric growth, providing a transcriptional framework for this process.

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.

This paper proposes 'Longevitomics' as a unified systems-science framework for studying healthy longevity, arguing that its determinants are currently fragmented across separate molecular layers (genomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome, digital phenotyping, AI). It defines the 'Longevitome' as the dynamic architecture integrating these layers, aiming to enable better modeling and prediction of healthy longevity.

Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.

Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that host-like temperature (37°C) enables pathogenic Leptospira to take up and metabolize glucose, challenging the long-held view that this bacterium relies almost exclusively on fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.

This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from lab studies to field-scale soil bioremediation by integrating mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives. It identifies key barriers limiting field performance and proposes evidence-based design principles for engineering plant-microbe-soil consortia. The work is a synthesis rather than new experimental data, aimed at guiding practical deployment of nature-inspired remediation strategies.

Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) 2026-11-02 Medium

scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.

The authors present scPhyloGRN, a method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by incorporating the lineage topology of cellular phylogenies. By using shared ancestry to disentangle expression variation due to cell state from that due to lineage history, the approach aims to produce more accurate gene-level regulatory inference. The abstract introduces the problem and method but does not report specific results.

Hearing research 2026-11-02 Medium

A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.

This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging mouse cochlea, tracking how different cell types change across the lifespan. It identifies two phases of age-related inflammation (inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication, gene regulatory networks, and bulk cross-cohort validation into one temporal framework.

Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.

This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 correlate with semen quality in rams, using ejaculates from five animals assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis. The authors combined experimental expression measurements with gene regulatory network analysis to identify potential upstream regulators of protamine genes. The findings suggest that protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams, extending observations from other species to this livestock context.

Bio Systems 2026-11-01 Medium

Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.

The authors propose a meta-learning approach to gene regulatory network inference that resolves disagreements between ten existing methods by training a gradient-boosted classifier on their raw edge scores, allowing the weight given to each method to vary per regulator-target pair. They also introduce a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the arbitration approach aims to outperform both single-method selection and simple averaging.

Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.

This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors report a high-quality annotated genome (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and identify coordinated regulatory networks involving 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEA proteins, suggesting synergistic roles in salt tolerance.

Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.

This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes over 113 days of culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs that drive maturation. TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.

This review argues that TREM2 acts as a central molecular hub governing macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the simple M1/M2 classification. It emphasizes that the timing of TREM2 signaling and the diversity of macrophage states create therapeutic opportunities, framing immune-metabolic crosstalk as a key driver of pathogenesis.

Archives of toxicology 2026-11-01 Medium

Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.

This review argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs, quantitative causal inference methods, and network-based approaches—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms. The paper provides guidance for toxicologists on operationalizing causal assessment in systems-level toxicology.

Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.

This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis reveals dynamic regulatory transitions during injury and identifies candidate genes with renoprotective potential. The work provides a temporal map of molecular events underlying cisplatin nephrotoxicity and regeneration.

Cell systems 2026-10-21 Medium

Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.

This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, and shows that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, such as oscillations coexisting with multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'dynamical zoo' of emergent behaviors and assess their robustness. The work challenges the traditional separation of studying multistability and oscillations in isolation, highlighting multifunctionality in gene regulatory networks.

Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.

It aims to robustly identify heterogeneity in communication pathways across cells and link these signals to downstream gene regulatory effects on cell fate. The method addresses the challenge of studying how communication operates across biological scales.

Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

This review argues that AI-generated predictions of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities are fundamentally different from experimentally confirmed ones, yet the field often treats them as interchangeable. It calls for clearer evidentiary standards when using machine learning and genome-scale models to identify synthetic lethal metabolic targets for precision oncology.

ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models.

Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.

The authors propose the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework to explain why individuals with similar genetic and environmental backgrounds can develop divergent immune-mediated phenotypes. They argue that immune outcomes reflect trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints, and that this framing can help integrate systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic data into clinically actionable reasoning.
